nodes.title: Zahorski's negative answer to Ulam's perfect set problem

nodes.summary: A set $s \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ is perfect if it is closed, nonempty, and has no isolated points: every $x \in s$ lies in the closure of $s \setminus \{x\}$.
nodes.title: Perfect sets of real numbers

nodes.summary: Ulam's Problem 17.1 from the Scottish Book: for every continuous `f` on `[0, 1]`, do there exist a perfect set `C` in `[0, 1]` and an analytic function `φ` with `f x = φ x` for every `x ∈ C`? The claim is stated for `C ^ ∞` functions, which is the case refuted by Zahorski's construction.
nodes.title: Ulam's problem on analytic agreement on a perfect set
